decisions.reason: Report identifies node.exe PID 42432 in running-processes.txt as the dsh web host that loaded koffi.node at startup, and explains that Windows holds the loaded native .node file locked/mapped until that process exits, so npm's copyfile fails with EBUSY. Also correctly rules out PID 23920 (the installer) as the holder.

Report explains a browser refresh only reloads the SPA and reconnects while the host process keeps koffi mapped, and gives an ordered stop-host → install → verify-restart procedure (steps 1-3 in section 3). It targets dsh-derived processes via tasklist rather than prescribing killing every Node process.

Report grounds the mechanism in npm-dist-tags.txt: unpinned install resolves to latest (0.1.1-rc.2) while alpha points to 0.1.2-alpha.5, and explicitly states an unpinned install neither preserves the installed version nor reaches the alpha line, correctly framing the alpha.4-to-rc.2 change as a downgrade.

Report provides npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.2-alpha.5 @deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui after stopping the host, verification via dsh --version expecting 0.1.2-alpha.5, and restart. The @alpha tag is mentioned only as a mutable alternative, not a replacement for the exact-version command.

Section 4 tells README authors to pin the exact tested core version whenever an install command also installs dsh, warns that unpinned specs silently follow latest over an existing prerelease, and recommends separating plugin install from dsh upgrade plus a version-check step; the quoted unpinned command is presented as the bad example, not endorsed.
